A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEMO study. All 33 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including Appendices A–E, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original NEMO evaluations on nine benchmarks, component ablations, extraction-consistency measurements, and failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, targeted ablations, simulator-generation evaluations, and repeated-run variability measurements.

M1.justification: The extraction, retrieval, solver recommendation, simulation, optimizer consensus, and asymmetric validation procedures remain unchanged. The new Workspace-State terminology explains an architecture already documented in v1, including its shared workspace and executable examples. Appendix E's prompts and code examples are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine optimization benchmarks and OptMATH training examples for memory. The added studies examine existing simulation and optimization components on retained benchmarks or subsets; they introduce no new domain, problem family, or input environment.

E2.justification: V2 adds a Best-of-5 ACA comparator on BWOR and OptMATH-Bench using Claude 4.5 Sonnet (Section 4.5, Table 3). The comparison methods and their participation in the original Table 1 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The headline evaluation protocol is retained. New protocols include single-shot simulator/optimizer Pass@1 on 100 human-verified OptiBench problems, a reportedly compute-matched comparison selecting the best objective from five ACA calls, and a fixed-Gurobi control on 133 OptiBench problems. These are additional experimental designs, not revisions to the original headline settings.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands tests of the architectural rationale: Table 2 extends component ablations to MAMO-Complex and NLP4LP; Sections 4.3–4.5 add an IndustryOR instance-level failure comparison, simulator-versus-optimizer generation analysis, and simulator removal from the complete system. Appendix B.6 isolates solver recommendation, and Section 6 adds latency profiling.

E5.justification: V1 reports extraction-consistency statistics but explicitly omits end-to-end variability reporting. V2 newly reports five independent evaluations on BWOR and ComplexOR, with standard deviations of 1.3% and 2.5%, respectively. Headline Table 1 still lacks uncertainty estimates, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are added: simulator/optimizer Pass@1 of 97%/87%, Best-of-5 accuracies of 79.3% on BWOR and 62.7% on OptMATH-Bench, and new component-ablation outcomes. The corresponding NEMO Sonnet 4.5 scores of 86.6%/68.1% already appeared in v1. Appendix D/Figure 6 revises IndustryOR correct models from 66 to 63 and constraint errors from 8 to 11, aligning the success count with the retained headline result.

T1.justification: The retrieval scoring, MBR utilities, consensus rules, validation equations, and evaluation formula remain unchanged. The new discussion of formulation correctness is a conceptual limitation, and the simulation-complexity comparison is empirical; neither introduces a formal proof or revised mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: V1's abstract explicitly advertises both user-collaborative and autonomous operation; v2 omits that operating-mode claim. The central ACA-based contributions and the conclusion's claim of first or tied-first performance on eight benchmarks under at least one evaluation setting remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of IndustryOR's zero marginal simulator gain, attributes gains to architectural feedback using new controls, and explicitly acknowledges that objective agreement does not establish formulation correctness. It also argues that curation is unnecessary for the headline conclusions. That last discussion overstates the evidence: Appendix A.2.4 claims eight standard-benchmark wins or ties, whereas Table 1 supports seven.

D1.justification: The promised post-review artifact link becomes a specific HuggingFace address for intermediate outputs. V2 additionally discloses error-blind curation and a latency breakdown of approximately 55% ACA reasoning, 32% validation/orchestration, and 13% initialization. Global hyperparameters and appendix implementation examples remain unchanged; the linked resource's availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1 and 5.2 sharpen NEMO's positioning through an explicit Workspace-State versus message-passing distinction, emphasizing shared executable artifacts and avoiding schema negotiation. This refines the existing comparison with critic-based systems without substantially expanding the literature review; most bibliography edits update publication details.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the abstract, rewrites selected opportunities, ablation, and positioning paragraphs, and adds focused experimental and limitation subsections. It also updates equal-contribution, affiliation, and publication information. The overall narrative order and extensive implementation appendix are retained.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 2, adds the compute-matched Table 3, and redraws Figure 6 with revised failure flows. Existing appendix tables and figures shift with text reflow and renumbering. Figures 1–5 retain identical image content, and the overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new controls and targeted ablations better support architectural attribution, while repeated-run reporting, artifact access information, and the formulation-correctness limitation improve transparency. The IndustryOR correction also resolves an inconsistency with Table 1. These benefits are tempered by unspecified numerical token budgets for the claimed compute match and Appendix A.2.4's incorrect eight-standard-benchmark claim. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
